question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable exec approval timeout, and if so what public key, precedence, maximum, and fail-closed semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing how long pending host-exec approvals remain actionable is a security-boundary and public-config decision that code review cannot choose safely.

options.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
options.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with a conservative maximum, validation, docs, and focused tests across every approval registration and wait path.

options.title: Keep the fixed 30-minute default
options.body: Leave the current fixed behavior as the only supported approval window and close duplicate configurability requests as not planned.

options.title: Improve operator recovery only
options.body: Address missed approvals through notices, Control UI recovery, or setup hints without adding a new timeout configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded timeout contract
recommendation.body: Add one maintainer-approved key with a conservative maximum, validation, docs, and focused tests across every approval registration and wait path.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeout history and current exec approval security/config ownership point most strongly to steipete for the product/security contract decision.
